title: Distribute Money to Maximum Children
statement:
You hold `money` dollars and must hand them out to `children` children, each child getting a whole number of dollars. A handout is allowed only when:

- every dollar is given away,
- each child gets at least 1 dollar,
- no child ends up with exactly 4 dollars.

Over all allowed handouts, find the largest number of children that can receive exactly 8 dollars and return it. If no allowed handout exists, return `-1`.
notes:
## Intuition

Every child needs at least 1 dollar, so hand that out first; after it, turning a child into an "eight" costs exactly 7 more dollars. Making as many eights as possible is clearly best, and only two leftover situations can break a rule. A slower route is to try every count `k` from `children` down to `0` and test whether the rest can be shared legally.

## Approach

1. If `money < children`, someone gets nothing, so return `-1`.
2. Give every child 1 dollar; `extra` is what remains.
3. Make `eights = min(floor(extra / 7), children)` children reach 8, and take `7 * eights` out of `extra`.
4. Let `others` be the children who are not eights. Fix the two bad cases:
   - `others === 0` but dollars remain: they must go to one of the eights, which stops being 8.
   - `others === 1` and `extra === 3`: that child would hold exactly 4, so give up one eight; the two children then share 12 dollars, for example 1 and 11.
5. In every other case the others can absorb `extra` (it is below 7), so return `eights`.

## Example 1, step by step

`money = 20`, `children = 3`. Since 20 >= 3, give 1 each: `extra = 17`. Then `eights = min(2, 3) = 2` and `extra = 17 - 14 = 3`. One child is left (`others = 1`) and it would get `1 + 3 = 4`, which is banned, so `eights` drops to `1`. The answer is `1` (for instance 8, 9 and 3).

## Complexity

- Time: O(1): a few arithmetic steps.
- Space: O(1).

## Pitfalls

- Cap `eights` at `children`; with lots of money every child could be an eight, yet the surplus still has to go somewhere.
- A leftover of 3 is only a problem when exactly one child remains; with two or more, share it as 2 and 1.
- With `extra` below 7 and one child left, that child never reaches 8 by accident, so no other case needs fixing.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `extra` | dollars left after every child got 1 (later, after the eights got their 7) |
| `eights` | children receiving exactly 8 dollars |
| `others` | children who are not eights |

narration.2: Every child needs at least one dollar; with fewer dollars than children that is impossible.
narration.3: No allowed handout exists, so report -1.
narration.5: Give each child its first dollar; extra is what is still to hand out.
narration.6: Each eight needs 7 more dollars; make as many as the money and the number of children allow.
narration.7: Remove the dollars spent on topping the eights up to 8.
narration.8: Count the children who did not become eights.
narration.9: Everyone is an eight but dollars are left over, so one eight must take them.
narration.10: That child is no longer an eight.
narration.11: A single remaining child would receive 1 + 3 = 4 dollars, which is not allowed.
narration.12: Give up one eight so two children can share the 12 dollars legally.
narration.14: Any other leftover fits on the remaining children, so this is the maximum.
